DOCUMENT LITERACY
HOW TO READ A BITUMEN CERTIFICATE OF ANALYSIS (COA)

LAST REVIEWED SEPTEMBER 10, 2026 · PETROBIND EXPORT DESK

A Certificate of Analysis (COA) is only useful to a buyer who knows what its numbers mean. This guide walks through the values most commonly reported on a bitumen COA and what each one tells you about the shipment.

Request Bitumen Quote
View Bitumen Grades
PENETRATION AND SOFTENING POINT

Penetration (measured in dmm, tenths of a millimeter) indicates hardness — lower penetration means a harder bitumen. Softening point (°C) shows the temperature at which the bitumen starts to soften. Together, these two values are the primary way a penetration-grade bitumen (e.g. 60/70) is identified and verified against the ordered grade.

DUCTILITY, FLASH POINT, AND SOLUBILITY

Ductility (cm) measures how far the bitumen can stretch before breaking — relevant to flexibility and crack resistance. Flash point (°C) is a safety figure, showing the temperature at which vapors could ignite; it should be comfortably above expected handling and application temperatures. Solubility (%) confirms purity — how much of the sample dissolves in a solvent, checking for unwanted residue or contamination.

Penetration & softening point — confirms the grade.

Ductility — confirms flexibility.

Flash point — confirms safe handling temperature margin.

Solubility — confirms purity.

MATCHING THE COA TO YOUR ORDER

Before approving a shipment, compare the COA's actual tested values against the grade's specification range (from the PDS or the relevant ASTM/EN standard) — not just the grade name. A COA that lists a grade name but omits actual test values, or shows values with no reference method, is a red flag worth querying before payment.
